idea-plugin.name: Git Worktree Sport
idea-plugin.description:
Create and manage Git worktrees without leaving your IDE. Keep parallel tasks in separate working directories while sharing one Git repository. Git Worktree Sport is free and has no purchase flow.

Git Worktree Sport

One repository. Parallel workspaces. Inspect worktrees across projects open in the IDE, create a workspace from a branch, and manage its lifecycle with explicit safety checks.

Get started

  1. Install the plugin and restart the IDE. Open a Git project with the IDE's Git integration enabled.
  2. Choose Git > Worktree Sport > Refresh to open the worktree manager.
  3. Right-click empty space in the worktree list. Search or scroll through local and remote branches, click a branch, then choose Create Worktree... in its submenu. You can also use this action in the IDE's Git Branches popup.
  4. Choose a creation mode, enter a destination or click Browse..., then create. The parent folder must exist and the destination must not already exist. Editing a new branch name updates the suggested folder until you customize it; Reset path restores the suggestion.
  5. After creation, choose Open Project to use the IDE's normal project-opening flow, or close the dialog to reveal the new worktree with a two-second blue background highlight.

Choose how to create

  • Existing branch: Check out the selected local branch. Remote selections reuse an existing local branch with the matching name or create a tracking branch.
  • New branch: Specify an unused new branch name and select a starting local or remote branch. An explicit advanced option accepts another Git reference, tag or commit.
  • Detached HEAD: Inspect a commit without attaching the new workspace to a branch.
  • Orphan branch: Start a branch without inherited commit history, subject to your installed Git version's support.
  • Do not check out files: An optional advanced setting for creating registration without populating files, for workflows such as sparse checkout. It is off by default and unavailable in orphan mode.

Parallel mode: When creating a new branch, enable this option to place it under the configurable prefix (default sync-git/). The prefix appears separately from the editable branch name and is applied only to newly created branches. Choose any existing local/remote branch or commit as the start point, including a maintenance branch from another release line. Git prevents the same branch from being checked out in multiple worktrees, so open the resulting worktree path directly in a separate IDE or coding-agent session instead of using Switch Branch from another worktree. Commit normally, then merge or cherry-pick the changes later. Existing-branch checkout and Detached HEAD do not use a new-branch prefix.

Create from a worktree row: The first context-menu action creates a new branch and worktree from that row's branch, not whichever branch is open in this IDE. This shortcut offers New branch and Detached HEAD, omitting Existing branch and Orphan. The general Create Worktree entry retains all four modes. Modes are arranged horizontally. Before creation, existing target paths and conflicting new branch names are reported together; each invalid field has a light-red outline until that field is edited.

Understand the worktree list

Repositories show registered-worktree counts. Each worktree has a compact status badge. Expand it to see its type, bare state, actual Git lock state, branch, full HEAD, folder creation time, and complete path. Duplicate names are grouped, with eight-character HEAD suffixes to distinguish children. Missing or prunable paths are marked.

Double-clicking expands or collapses a node. Expanded worktrees provide Open Worktree and Open Folder buttons; an already-open worktree does not offer another Open Worktree action. Right-click a detail row to copy only its value. Refresh reads local metadata and does not fetch remote branches.

Manage safely

  • Open Worktree: Open or import the project through the IDE. Open Folder: Open the directory in the operating system's file manager.
  • Lock / Unlock: Set or remove Git's retention marker. A lock prevents pruning of its registration; it does not make files read-only.
  • Repair: Ask Git to repair administrative links after directories have been moved outside the plugin. It updates metadata, not source files or commits.
  • Prune or Delete: A valid worktree offers Delete; a missing or prunable registration offers Prune instead. Prune previews repository-wide stale registrations and does not delete existing directories. Delete removes a linked directory and its registration. Modified or untracked files require a separate confirmation before force removal.
  • Move: Ask Git to move a linked worktree and update registration. The destination must not exist and its parent must exist.

Protection and menu settings: The main worktree and worktrees open as projects in this IDE session cannot be pruned, moved, deleted, locked, or unlocked from the manager. This protection is independent of branch names and does not create a Git lock. Truly Git-locked worktrees also hide Move and Delete. Settings offer an optional global Hide Move and Delete checkbox, off by default. It affects only menu visibility and never weakens protection. The main worktree always hides Move, Delete, Lock and Unlock because Git does not support those operations on its primary working tree. Other worktrees show Lock or Unlock according to their Git lock state, disabled when protected. Repair is unaffected; Prune appears only for eligible missing or stale registrations. High-risk operations have confirmations, and running operations show a blocking progress state. Deletion shows elapsed time and a longer-wait explanation after 30 seconds, without a false completion percentage or unsafe mid-operation cancellation.

Feedback: The settings dialog includes a Submit feedback button that opens this project's GitHub Issues page in your browser.

Creation conflicts: Missing-directory registrations can be cleaned after confirmation before retrying. A branch checked out elsewhere requires explicit force confirmation. Active worktrees are not duplicated, and non-empty directories are never overwritten.

Language and translation tools

Use the settings button beside Refresh to follow the IDE language or select a bundled language. The current release includes eleven language packs: English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese (HKSAR), Traditional Chinese (Taiwan Province), Japanese, Korean, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), and Russian. Labels display the running IDE's product name rather than assuming a particular IDE.

The translation editor opens at the current language. Switch tabs, edit values while keys remain read-only, or search with Ctrl+F / Search..., optionally including keys. Import and export key=value text with checks for missing, duplicate, and unknown keys. Add a language with +, double-click a tab to rename it, and right-click a user-added tab to delete it after confirmation. Discarding an unsaved session restores all its changes, including added tabs.

Language names live in a separate JSON catalog. The language-list editor lets you rename entries, import/export names, or start adding a language. Existing translations and custom names are retained when new bundled languages are added.

Requirements and boundaries

Requires a compatible IntelliJ Platform build, the Git plugin, and an installed Git executable configured in the IDE. This build targets platform 262.9437.185 or newer and was built against Android Studio Panda 3. Android Studio is available for macOS, and the plugin uses cross-platform IDE and Java APIs; however, this release has not been runtime-tested on macOS. Other products and versions require separate compatibility verification. Git operations run locally; the plugin does not provide hosting, fetching, merging, rebasing, or deployment features.

See the listing's Media section for walkthrough screenshots. Screenshots are reference images supplied by the author; some show the earlier two-language interface. The current release includes eleven language packs.
idea-plugin.change-notes:
1.0.4

  • Added optional Parallel mode for creating isolated, namespaced branches from any selected start branch or commit. The prefix is configurable and applies only to newly created branches.

Added Create Worktree from this branch to worktree row menus, horizontal creation modes, source-branch selection, automatic destination naming with a reset option, and field-specific path/branch conflict feedback.

  • Added optional global Move/Delete hiding, off by default, with consistent behavior in the Git menu and tree popup. Removed the misleading main-worktree action setting; unsupported Move/Delete/Lock/Unlock actions remain hidden for the main worktree.
  • Linked worktrees show Lock/Unlock according to Git state, disabled when protected; Repair and eligible Prune actions are independent of the visibility preference.
  • Added a settings shortcut to GitHub Issues and updated all ten language packs.
  • Added elapsed time and longer-wait feedback to deletion dialogs while retaining all execution protections.

1.0.3.101

  • Kept the Worktree Sport tool window available during indexing, so its localized loading message appears instead of the IDE's English placeholder.

1.0.3.100

  • Replaced deprecated project-root and startup APIs to improve compatibility with newer IntelliJ Platform builds.
  • Kept the worktree list in a localized loading state while project initialization or indexing is still in progress.

1.0.3

  • Improved worktree action availability and validation for missing, invalid, locked, and currently open worktrees.
  • Hardened Git worktree metadata parsing and added regression coverage for cleanup and protection rules.
  • Added automatic refresh after IDE initialization and reliable context-menu targeting across the full worktree row.
  • Added optional list instructions and a setting to show protected high-risk actions as disabled entries with their protection reason.

1.0.2

  • Kept both language editor actions visible in a second row aligned with the language selector.

1.0.1

  • Replaced a deprecated repository chooser with the IDE's native popup chooser.
  • Limited the Windows Git long-path setting to Windows hosts and added macOS Android Studio path defaults for development builds.
  • Updated setup instructions and compatibility notes; macOS runtime behavior still requires device verification.
